structure: Overall prediction: the line will get worse before it gets better.
Explain why: one open window, the customer with a jar of coins, the impatient man at almost 1 p.m.
Positive turn: the second teller with the 'Open' sign.
Two side predictions: the card left in the ATM; the child pulling the rope and the tilting post.
modelAnswer: From the look of things, this credit union is going to get even more chaotic before it gets better. Right now, only one teller window is open, and an older gentleman is there with a huge jar of coins, so the people in line will be waiting for quite a while. The man in the dark suit is already checking his watch, and since it's almost one o'clock, he might give up and head back to work. Luckily, a second teller is putting an 'Open' sign up at one of the closed windows, so the line should start moving faster soon. Meanwhile, at the ATM, a man has just taken his cash and is walking away, but his bank card is still sticking out of the machine. The woman at the ATM is pointing at it, so she'll probably call him back. Finally, a little kid at the end of the line is pulling on the rope between the posts, and one post is already leaning over, so I wouldn't be surprised if the whole row comes down like dominoes.

commonMistakes: Nhầm 'line' (hàng người xếp hàng, tiếng Anh Canada) với 'queue'; cả hai đều được, nhưng 'line up / wait in line' tự nhiên hơn ở Canada.
Dùng 'forget' sai thì: 'he forgets his card' khi kể dự đoán → 'he has left his card in the machine'.
Không nói kết cục tích cực nào; dự đoán cân bằng (cả xấu lẫn tốt) nghe tự nhiên và thuyết phục hơn.
